property_summary: For any caller and amount, contract C accepts fallback calls only when msg.value == 10 ether and then updates pastBlockTime to a value greater than previous; the mutant that requires 5 ether will accept different amounts, so there exist inputs where the reference rejects but the mutant accepts (or vice versa) — specifically, for fuzzed amount not equal to 10 ether the reference revert while mutant may accept when amount == 5 ether.

For any caller and any block time, when calling fallback with exactly 10 ether the reference contract always ensures pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the previous stored value (monotonic increase), whereas the mutant can overwrite pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, breaking monotonicity.

For any call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, the reference contract only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the previous stored value (so pastBlockTime never decreases or stays the same across such valid calls), while the mutant can overwrite pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, breaking that monotonicity.

For any call to fallback supplying exactly 10 ether, the reference contract only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than its previous stored value (so pastBlockTime after the call is equal to block.timestamp+1 only if block.timestamp exceeded the prior stored time); the mutant removes the time check and can overwrite pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, violating this conditional-update rule.

For any call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, the reference C only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the currently stored pastBlockTime-1 (i.e., pastBlockTime after the call is either unchanged or becomes block.timestamp+1 only if block.timestamp > previous pastBlockTime-1); the mutant removes that time check and can set pastBlockTime = block.timestamp+1 even when block.timestamp is not greater, so there exists an input (sequence of calls with same timestamp) that makes the mutant change pastBlockTime while the reference does not.

For any call to fallback sending exactly 10 ether, the reference contract only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than its stored value (so calling twice at the same timestamp will only update once), whereas the mutant removes that time check and can update pastBlockTime on a second call at the same timestamp — the property: two consecutive valid fallback calls from the same caller at the same block.timestamp must leave pastBlockTime unchanged after the second call in the reference but may change in the mutant.

After any successful fallback call that requires msg.value == 10 ether and passes the timestamp check, the contract's public pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the block.timestamp observed before the call returns; the mutant that writes pastBlockTime = block.timestamp can make pastBlockTime equal to block.timestamp and thus violate this property for some inputs.

After any successful fallback call that accepts 10 ether and the precondition block.timestamp > pastBlockTime holds, the reference contract always stores pastBlockTime strictly greater than the current block.timestamp (it sets pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1), whereas the mutant that sets pastBlockTime = block.timestamp can make pastBlockTime equal to block.timestamp for some inputs, violating the strictness.

After any successful payable fallback call, C.pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the block.timestamp observed immediately before the call returned; the mutant that writes block.timestamp (not +1) can make pastBlockTime equal to that timestamp for some inputs, violating the strict > relation.

For every call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether and occurs at a strictly later timestamp than the previous call, the reference contract only drains its balance when block.number % 15 == 0, so after such a call either address(c).balance == 0 iff block.number % 15 == 0; the mutant inverts the conditional and thus for some block numbers this property is violated (balance drained at block.number % 15 != 0).

Whenever fallback is called with msg.value == 10 ether and block.number % 15 == 0, the reference contract transfers the entire contract balance to the caller so that address(c).balance becomes 0 afterwards; the mutant that transfers only half breaks this by leaving a non-zero balance for some inputs.

For every call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime where block.number % 15 == 0, the reference contract transfers its entire balance to the caller so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards; the mutant that transfers only half will leave a non-zero balance for some such inputs.

For any admissible call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether and occurs at a strictly greater timestamp than pastBlockTime and with block.number % 15 == 0, the reference contract forwards its entire balance to the caller so that address(c).balance == 0 afterwards; the mutant that forwards only half will leave a non-zero contract balance for some such inputs.

For any call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether and occurs at a strictly greater timestamp than pastBlockTime, if block.number % 15 == 0 then the reference contract drains its entire balance to the caller (so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant that transfers only half will leave a non-zero contract balance for some such inputs.

For any call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether and occurs at a later timestamp than pastBlockTime, if block.number % 15 == 0 then the reference contract drains its entire balance (so address(c).balance == 0) after the call; the mutant that transfers only half can leave a non-zero balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

After any fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether and when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference C updates pastBlockTime to a strictly larger value (pastBlockTime >= old + 1), whereas the mutant fails to update pastBlockTime causing it to remain unchanged for some inputs.
